title: Joseph and His Brothers
bigQuestion: What does the story say happens when someone chooses to forgive?

story.title: The Coat Everyone Wanted
story.kicker: A father gives one son a special coat, and eleven brothers watch.
paragraphs: Jacob has twelve sons. He loves Joseph the most. Joseph is one of the youngest. Genesis tells this story. One day Jacob gives Joseph a coat. It is a special coat. Some Bibles say it has many colors. Some say it has long sleeves.
Joseph puts the coat on. He walks past his brothers. The coat is bright in the sun. The brothers look at each other. Nobody gave them a coat like that.
Joseph has dreams, too. He tells his brothers about them. In one dream, their bundles of wheat bow down to his bundle. The brothers do not like that dream at all.
The story says the brothers began to hate Joseph. They could not say one kind word to him. This is where the trouble starts. But it is not where the story ends.
story.think: How do you think the brothers felt when they saw the coat?

lessons.title: Joseph's Special Coat
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jacob loved Joseph most and gave him a special coat.
reading: Jacob had twelve sons. Joseph was next to the youngest. The story says Jacob loved Joseph more than the others. That was a problem.
Jacob gave Joseph a special *coat*. The King James Bible calls it a coat of many colors. Other Bibles call it a long coat with sleeves. Either way, it was fancy.
The brothers saw the coat. The story says they were jealous. *Jealous* means you want what someone else has. They stopped being nice to Joseph.

words.d: a piece of clothing you wear on top; Joseph's was a special one
wanting what someone else has, and feeling upset about it

look.title: One Coat, Eleven Brothers
look.text: Look at twelve boys in a field. Eleven wear plain brown coats. One wears a coat that is bright and long. His father pats him on the back. The other boys stand with their arms crossed.
look.prompt: If you were one of the eleven, what would you want to say to your father?

check.q: Who gave Joseph the coat?
check.why: Genesis says Jacob, Joseph's father, gave him the special coat.

check.q: What does jealous mean?
check.why: Jealous means you want what someone else has. The brothers wanted a coat like Joseph's.

check.q: How many sons did Jacob have?
check.why: Jacob had twelve sons. Joseph was one of them.

lessons.title: Dreams That Bow Down
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Joseph dreamed his family would bow to him, and it made his brothers angry.
reading: Joseph had two dreams. In the first, he and his brothers tied up bundles of wheat. The story says his bundle stood up. The other bundles bowed down to it.
In the second dream, the sun, the moon and eleven stars bowed to Joseph. He told his family. His father said, will we all *bow* to you?
The brothers got angrier. The story says they hated Joseph even more. Remember these dreams. They come back later in the story.

words.d: to bend low to show that someone is important

look.title: What Bowed Down
rows: Bundles of wheat in dream one
Suns and moons in dream two
look.unit: things that bowed in the story
look.prompt: Joseph had eleven brothers. What do the eleven stars stand for?

check.q: What bowed down in Joseph's first dream?
check.why: Genesis 37 says the brothers' bundles of wheat bowed to Joseph's bundle.

check.q: How many stars were in the second dream?
check.why: The story says eleven stars bowed, one for each brother.

check.q: How did the brothers feel about the dreams?
check.why: The story says the dreams made the brothers hate Joseph even more.

lessons.title: Sold by His Brothers
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the brothers sold Joseph, and traders took him to Egypt.
reading: One day the brothers were far away with the sheep. Jacob sent Joseph to check on them. The brothers saw him coming. They made a bad plan.
They took his coat. They threw him in a dry hole. Then some *traders* came by. The story says the brothers sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver.
The traders took Joseph to *Egypt*. The brothers dipped the coat in goat blood. They showed it to Jacob. Jacob thought Joseph was dead. He cried and cried.

words.d: people who travel and buy and sell things
a land by the Nile River where Joseph was taken

look.title: Two Brothers Speak Up
look.text: The story says two brothers did not want Joseph hurt. Reuben said, do not kill him. Put him in the hole instead. He planned to come back for Joseph. Judah said, let us not hurt him. Let us sell him instead.
look.prompt: Did Reuben and Judah do enough to help Joseph? What else could they have done?

check.q: What did the brothers do to Joseph?
check.why: Genesis 37 says the brothers sold Joseph to traders for silver.

check.q: Where did the traders take Joseph?
check.why: The story says the traders took Joseph down to Egypt.

check.q: What did Jacob think when he saw the bloody coat?
check.why: The brothers made it look like a wild animal got Joseph. Jacob thought he was dead.

lessons.title: Pharaoh's Strange Dreams
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Joseph explained Pharaoh's dreams: seven fat years, then seven thin years.
reading: In Egypt, Joseph had hard years. He worked as a servant. He even went to jail for something he did not do. But the story says he could explain dreams.
The king of Egypt was called *Pharaoh*. He had two dreams. Seven fat cows came out of the river. Then seven skinny cows ate them up. Nobody could explain it.
Joseph was brought from jail. He said, the dreams mean the same thing. Seven good years of food are coming. Then seven years with no food. Get ready now.

words.d: the name for the king of Egypt

look.title: Fat Cows, Thin Cows
look.text: The story says Pharaoh dreamed he stood by the river. Seven fat cows came up and ate grass. Then seven thin cows came up. The thin cows ate the fat cows. Pharaoh woke up.
look.cite: Genesis 41, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why would thin cows eating fat cows be a scary dream for a king?

check.q: What is a Pharaoh?
check.why: Pharaoh is the name for the king of Egypt in the story.

check.q: What did the seven fat cows mean, in Joseph's words?
check.why: Joseph said the fat cows meant seven good years of food.

check.q: Where was Joseph before he saw Pharaoh?
check.why: The story says Joseph was in jail. Pharaoh sent for him to explain the dreams.

lessons.title: Saving Up Food
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Pharaoh put Joseph in charge, and Joseph stored food for the hungry years.
reading: Pharaoh liked Joseph's plan. The story says he made Joseph his top helper. Only Pharaoh was more important. Joseph got a ring, fine clothes and a chariot.
For seven years, the crops grew big. Joseph did not let people eat it all. He *stored* the extra grain in big buildings in every city.
Then the thin years came. No rain. No crops. People were hungry all over. But Egypt had food. The story says people came from far away to buy it.

words.d: to save something and keep it safe for later
seeds like wheat that people grind to make bread

look.title: Years of Food, Years of Hunger
look.prompt: Why was it smart to save grain in the good years?

check.q: What job did Pharaoh give Joseph?
check.why: Genesis 41 says Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all of Egypt.

check.q: What did Joseph do with the extra grain?
check.why: Joseph stored the grain so there would be food in the hungry years.

check.q: What happened in the thin years?
check.why: The story says no crops grew, and people were hungry everywhere.

lessons.title: The Brothers Come to Buy Food
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the brothers came to Egypt for food and did not know Joseph.
reading: Back in Canaan, Jacob's family was hungry too. Jacob sent ten sons to Egypt to buy grain. The youngest, Benjamin, stayed home.
The brothers came to the man in charge. They *bowed* low. It was Joseph! He knew them right away. But they did not know him. He wore Egyptian clothes now.
Joseph remembered his dreams. The bundles had bowed. Now his brothers bowed. He did not tell them who he was. Not yet.

words.d: bent down low to show respect
Jacob's youngest son and Joseph's little brother

look.title: Do You Know Me?
look.text: Look at ten tired men with empty sacks. They bow to a man in fine Egyptian clothes. He wears gold. He looks at each face for a long time. One of them has a gray beard now. The man in gold knows every name.
look.prompt: Why do you think Joseph did not tell them who he was right away?

check.q: Why did the brothers go to Egypt?
check.why: The story says the family was hungry, so Jacob sent the brothers to buy grain.

check.q: Did the brothers know the man was Joseph?
choices: No, they did not know him
check.why: Genesis 42 says Joseph knew them, but they did not know him.

check.q: Which brother stayed home?
check.why: Jacob kept Benjamin, the youngest, at home the first time.

lessons.title: Joseph Forgives
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Joseph forgave his brothers, and the whole family moved to Egypt.
reading: The brothers came back a second time with Benjamin. Joseph tested them. Judah spoke up. He offered to stay in Egypt instead of Benjamin.
Joseph could not hold it in. He sent his helpers out. He cried out loud. I am Joseph, he said. The brothers were scared. But Joseph said, do not be afraid.
To *forgive* means to let go of being angry. The story says Joseph forgave. He hugged his brothers. Then the whole family, and old Jacob, moved to Egypt.

words.d: to let go of being angry at someone who was unkind to you

look.title: You Meant It for Bad
look.text: After Jacob died, the brothers were scared again. The story says Joseph told them, do not be afraid. You meant to do me harm. But God meant it for good, to save many people. I will take care of you.
look.cite: Genesis 50, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Joseph says the bad thing turned into a good thing. What good thing?

check.q: What does forgive mean?
choices: To let go of being angry
check.why: To forgive is to let go of being angry at someone who hurt you.

check.q: What did Joseph tell his scared brothers?
check.why: Genesis says Joseph told them not to be afraid, and he took care of them.

check.q: Where did the whole family move at the end?
check.why: The story says Jacob and all his family moved to Egypt to be near Joseph.

review.why: Genesis 37 says Jacob gave Joseph a special coat.

review.q: What did the brothers get when they sold Joseph?
review.why: The story says the traders paid twenty pieces of silver.

review.q: Who had a dream about seven fat cows?
review.why: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, dreamed about the cows.

review.q: How many years of hunger did Joseph say were coming?
review.why: Joseph said seven good years, then seven years with no food.

review.q: Why did the brothers bow to Joseph in Egypt?
choices: He was in charge of the food
review.why: Joseph was the man in charge. They bowed to buy grain, not knowing him.

review.q: What did Joseph do when he told them who he was?
choices: Sent them to Canaan for good
review.why: Genesis 45 says Joseph forgave his brothers and hugged them.
